productTitle: Vintage Western Bolo Tie — v2 anti-AI editorial
authoredBy: in-chat scene design v2 — anti-AI realism formula baked into each prompt (editorial publication framing + concrete imperfections + reject cinematic AI balance + zero color cast + Kodak Portra 400 texture + atmospheric variation). 6 distinct editorial dialects: Garden & Gun, T Magazine, Cowboys & Indians, Wallpaper*, Kinfolk, Cereal.

scenes.prompt: Commissioned editorial photography for Garden & Gun magazine, two-page Southern-heritage spread; NOT a product render, NOT advertising, NOT stock. Aesthetic reference: Mark Hartman and Squire Fox. Captured on a Hasselblad H6D-100c with a Hasselblad HC 50mm f/3.5 lens at f/6.3. Composition feels inevitable, not staged — the bolo tie placed off-centre at the right-third rule-of-thirds line. A vintage walnut side table in a softly lit Southern library at late afternoon, framed at seated-reading eye-level slight three-quarter, the bolo tie lying coiled across the closed pages of a battered leather-bound family Bible with a frayed silk bookmark protruding, in the front-right of a 1:1 frame. Warm tungsten side light from a brass library lamp just out of frame at left, mixed with cool soft window light from frame-right. Style — a small stoneware tumbler holding three antique brass-nibbed fountain pens, a pair of worn reading glasses with one earpiece slightly bent, a folded handkerchief with faint laundry creases. Walls behind: deep forest-green-painted bookshelves with a row of mismatched cloth-bound spines. CONCRETE IMPERFECTIONS REQUIRED: thin dust film visible across the table edge catching the warm tungsten light as fine motes; a faint ring-mark from a long-gone tumbler on the table surface; the Bible's leather spine cracked along two visible creases; the bolo's leather cord shows one small crease where it has been knotted before; the brass tip aglet has a 1-2mm scratch visible from years of wear. REJECT CINEMATIC AI BALANCE: do NOT lift shadows to flat grey — the corners of the room fall away to genuine darkness with shadow detail intact; do NOT make the tungsten lamp a perfectly circular smooth glow — it has slight uneven bloom and clipping at the brightest filament. ZERO COLOR CAST: the warm 2700K tungsten stays local to the lamp side; the cool 7500K window light stays local to the right; walls and Bible cover read as their true colours, not a global warm tint. PHOTOGRAPHIC TEXTURE: visible Kodak Portra 400 film grain especially in shadow areas (organic, not pixelated), gentle 1-3% corner vignette, subtle f/6.3 depth-of-field falloff so the bookshelves behind go soft, 1-2 px chromatic aberration only at the brightest lamp edge. The bolo tie matches the variant reference image exactly — leather cord colour and pendant ornament as shown. Palette of forest green, walnut, warm tungsten amber, soft cream, faded brass, worn leather. No people, no alcohol.
accents: leather-bound family Bible with frayed silk bookmark
stoneware tumbler of antique brass-nibbed pens
worn reading glasses with bent earpiece
brass library lamp casting tungsten side light

scenes.prompt: Commissioned editorial photography for T Magazine (New York Times Style); NOT a product render, NOT advertising, NOT stock. Aesthetic reference: Christopher Sturman and Aaron Tilley. Captured on a Hasselblad H6D-100c with a Hasselblad HC 80mm f/2.8 lens at f/5.6, shot directly overhead 90° so the bolo tie sits coiled inside a small chipped white ironstone bowl placed off-centre at the upper-left third of a 1:1 frame on a softly rumpled raw-linen surface in oat-cream tone. Compositionally asymmetric — the bowl up-left, props weight up-right, generous negative space at the lower-left. Soft cool overhead studio daylight from a single north-facing window, no fill. Style — the corner of a deeply folded chambray work shirt with a single button visible at frame-right, a small enamel-painted vintage state-pin (faded paint, hand-poured edges), a single dried sprig of mountain sage placed casually, and a tiny brass token engraved with a worn star. CONCRETE IMPERFECTIONS REQUIRED: the ironstone bowl has one tiny chip on its rim and two thin hairline crackle lines in the glaze; the linen has real visible creases and one small pulled thread loop; the chambray shirt shows soft wash-faded wear at the collar fold; the bolo's brass tip aglet shows a thumbnail-sized patina spot; one sage leaf is slightly curled and brittle. REJECT CINEMATIC AI BALANCE: do NOT distribute light evenly across the surface — the upper-left receives slightly more light than the lower-right; commit to the exposure so the cream linen does not go pure white. ZERO COLOR CAST: cool window light stays cool but does not tint the chambray or sage; surfaces reflect only what hits them. PHOTOGRAPHIC TEXTURE: visible Kodak Portra 400 film grain in the linen mid-tones (organic, fine), barely-noticeable 1-2% corner vignette, gentle f/5.6 falloff so the linen weave is razor sharp under the bowl and softer at the lower-left corner. The bolo tie matches the variant reference image exactly — leather cord colour and pendant ornament as shown. Palette of oat-cream linen, chambray faded blue, enamel red-and-yellow pin accent, dried sage green, soft brass. No people, no alcohol.
accents: chipped white ironstone bowl with hairline crackle

scenes.prompt: Commissioned editorial photography for Cowboys & Indians magazine, ranch-life feature; NOT a product render, NOT advertising, NOT stock. Aesthetic reference: Bruce Davidson documentary and Adam Jeppesen's still-lifes. Captured on a Hasselblad H6D-100c with a Hasselblad HC 50mm f/3.5 lens at f/5.6 at standing-adult chest-level slight three-quarter so the bolo tie hangs vertically from a hand-forged wrought-iron hat hook in the centre-right third of a 1:1 frame on a weathered vertical-plank barn wall. Warm late-afternoon raking light enters from a small unframed window outside the frame at upper-left — a single bright shaft of light crosses the planks diagonally, leaving the lower-right corner in genuine deep shadow. Style — a tan felt wide-brim cowboy hat hung on a second hook to the left (slightly tilted, brim asymmetric from years of wear), a hand-tooled leather belt with a brass star buckle coiled and hung on a third hook below, an unframed sepia-toned photograph of a horse pinned to the wall with a small tack. CONCRETE IMPERFECTIONS REQUIRED: the barn planks show two visible knots and three nailheads slightly proud of the wood, with hairline cracks running along the grain; the wrought-iron hooks show black paint chipped at the curve revealing rust beneath; the tan hat brim shows real wear-staining at the front pinch; the leather belt has visible scuff marks and one belt-hole stretched oval; the bolo's leather cord shows knotting creases. REJECT CINEMATIC AI BALANCE: the raking sunlight shaft is BRIGHT — let it slightly clip on the brightest plank; the lower-right corner stays in deep shadow with shadow detail (not lifted to grey); do not make the lighting even. ZERO COLOR CAST: warm raking 4000K daylight stays on the planks it touches; planks in shadow read true neutral weathered grey, no global warm tint. PHOTOGRAPHIC TEXTURE: visible Kodak Portra 400 film grain especially in the deep shadow areas (organic), 2-3% corner vignette, gentle f/5.6 falloff so the planks behind the hook go softer, 1-2 px chromatic aberration only on the brightest sunlit plank edge. The bolo tie matches the variant reference image exactly — leather cord colour and pendant ornament as shown. Palette of weathered barn-grey, sun-warmed amber raking light, tan felt, dark leather, oxidised iron, sepia photograph. No people, no alcohol.

scenes.prompt: Commissioned editorial photography for Wallpaper* magazine, design-object feature; NOT a product render, NOT advertising, NOT stock. Aesthetic reference: Aaron Tilley and Daniel Jackson studio still-lifes. Captured on a Hasselblad H6D-100c with a Hasselblad HC 120mm f/4 macro lens at f/4.5, shot at low 3/4 angle 20° above the surface so the bolo tie lies diagonally across a slab of weathered grey slate with the metal pendant rendered in sharp macro detail in the front-centre of a 1:1 frame, the leather cord falling away into deliberate soft focus toward the upper-left corner. Editorial macro composition — only the pendant ornament is razor sharp, everything else gradient-softens. Single soft directional studio light from camera-upper-left, gentle and committed to one exposure value. Style — a single small natural pebble placed at the back of the slate as the only secondary element, and the merest edge of a folded raw-linen cloth visible at the lower-left frame edge. CONCRETE IMPERFECTIONS REQUIRED: the slate slab shows real natural surface variation — one slightly chipped corner, fine layered cleavage lines, a single pale calcite vein running diagonally; the metal pendant ornament shows visible micro-scratches across its polished face, faint thumb-pressure tarnish on one edge, and small hand-tooling marks where the design was struck; the brass tip aglet shows real patina with a 1mm dent; the leather cord shows one small bead of natural oil sheen. REJECT CINEMATIC AI BALANCE: the highlight on the polished pendant face is allowed to slightly clip at its brightest specular hit — natural source clipping; the slate falls into committed shadow at the lower-right corner. ZERO COLOR CAST: cool studio daylight (5500K) stays neutral; warm leather cord reads warm, cool slate reads cool, no global wash. PHOTOGRAPHIC TEXTURE: Kodak Portra 400 grain visible in the slate mid-tones especially in shadow, organic and fine; 2% corner vignette; pronounced f/4.5 depth-of-field falloff (this is the most macro-shallow of the set); 1-2 px purple-cyan chromatic aberration ONLY at the brightest pendant specular highlight. The bolo tie matches the variant reference image exactly — leather cord colour and pendant ornament as shown, with EXTRA emphasis on the pendant detail. Palette of weathered slate grey, calcite white vein, soft metal patina, warm cord leather, raw linen cream. No people, no alcohol.

Commissioned editorial photography for Garden & Gun magazine, front-porch ritual feature; NOT a product render, NOT advertising, NOT stock. Aesthetic reference: Squire Fox and Annie Schlechter. Captured on a Hasselblad H6D-100c with a Hasselblad HC 80mm f/2.8 lens at f/5.6 at low porch-railing chest-level slight three-quarter so the bolo tie drapes naturally across the upturned brim of a worn straw cowboy hat sitting on a weathered cedar porch railing in the front-centre of a 1:1 frame. Warm golden hour low-sun raking light from camera-back-left, with a clear lens-flare-free presentation but distinct warm directional shadow. Style — one hand-thrown speckled-stoneware mug nearby (empty, no liquid, no alcohol) with visible thumb-glaze unevenness, a small dog-eared paperback Western novel folded face-down on the railing with the spine creased, and a single hand-rolled length of natural twine. Soft-focus background: a rolling hillside meadow with golden-hour grasses, and an asymmetric atmospheric sky with broken cumulus catching warm low-sun light from below — heavier cloud at upper-right, clear patch at upper-left, faint atmospheric haze at the horizon. CONCRETE IMPERFECTIONS REQUIRED: the cedar porch railing shows two real splits along its grain and a small chipped paint speck of faded sage where it was once painted; the straw cowboy hat shows real wear at the front pinch with one or two broken straw strands; the stoneware mug has a small hairline crackle line near the rim; the paperback shows real dog-ear creases and one yellowing edge; the bolo's leather cord shows one knotted crease. REJECT CINEMATIC AI BALANCE: commit to golden-hour exposure — the upper-right shoulder of the straw hat is BLOWN slightly in highlight; the front pinch of the hat falls into committed warm shadow; do NOT lift shadows; do not flatten the light. ZERO COLOR CAST: warm golden-hour light stays surface-local; the meadow grasses read warm where lit, cool where in self-shadow; the cedar railing reads its true weathered grey on the shadowed side. PHOTOGRAPHIC TEXTURE: Kodak Portra 400 grain visible in shadow areas, organic and fine; 2-3% corner vignette; f/5.6 falloff so the meadow goes gently soft; subtle 1-2 px warm chromatic aberration only at the brightest blown-highlight edge of the hat. ATMOSPHERIC SKY: asymmetric broken cumulus, heavier cover upper-right, clear at upper-left, warm underlit. The bolo tie matches the variant reference image exactly — leather cord colour and pendant ornament as shown. Palette of weathered cedar grey, sun-bleached straw, warm golden-hour amber, hand-thrown speckled stoneware, faded paperback brown. No people, no alcohol.
accents: worn straw cowboy hat brim with broken strands

scenes.prompt: Commissioned editorial photography for Kinfolk magazine, craft-object feature; NOT a product render, NOT advertising, NOT stock. Aesthetic reference: Aaron Tilley and Lasse Fløde. Captured on a Hasselblad H6D-100c with a Hasselblad HC 80mm f/2.8 lens at f/5.6 at slight high 3/4 angle 40° above the desk so the bolo tie sits unspooled along the length of an open hand-bound notebook in the right-third of a 1:1 frame, the leather cord crossing onto the desk surface. Compositionally asymmetric — bolo right, generous negative-space desk surface left. Soft natural cool window light from frame-upper-left as the only source, committed to one exposure. Style — handwritten field notes on creamy cotton-rag notebook paper in faded brown fountain-pen ink (legible-looking marks, not real readable text), a capped brass-and-wood fountain pen resting beside the notebook with the cap loose, a single sprig of dried sagebrush placed casually, a worn brass pocket compass with patina and a hairline crack in its glass face, and a small ironstone saucer holding two used pen nibs. CONCRETE IMPERFECTIONS REQUIRED: the notebook's hand-bound cotton-rag pages show real deckle edges and one small dog-ear; the desk surface (warm oak) shows faint ring-marks and pen-ink scratches accumulated over time; the fountain pen has worn brass at the clip; the compass glass has a real hairline crack; the sagebrush is dry and one stem is broken; the bolo's metal pendant has visible micro-scratches and faint thumb-tarnish where it has been worn. REJECT CINEMATIC AI BALANCE: the cool window light is committed — the upper-left of the notebook page is BRIGHTER than the lower-right corner; the desk in deep shadow goes properly dark, not lifted to grey; do not make exposure even. ZERO COLOR CAST: cool 5500K window light stays local to the upper-left; warm oak desk reads warm in shadow, cool where directly lit; no global tint. PHOTOGRAPHIC TEXTURE: Kodak Portra 400 grain across the desk mid-tones and shadow areas (organic, fine), 1-2% corner vignette, gentle f/5.6 depth-of-field falloff so the compass and saucer go softer than the notebook centre. Composition feels inevitable, not styled. The bolo tie matches the variant reference image exactly — leather cord colour and pendant ornament as shown. Palette of warm oak desk, cream notebook paper, faded brown fountain-ink, brass patina, dried sage green, soft cool window light. No people, no alcohol.
